nodes.title: RefMod identity preset
widgets_values:
# Character Replace example (RefMod identity + SAM3 masks)

## Quick start

1. Drop your source video into `ComfyUI/input` and point the timeline Source Video at it
   (currently `character_replace_source_example.mp4`).
2. `Load H3 RefMods` slot 1 = your character mod, `strength_1` 1.0, `copies_1` 1.
   Keep the mod images cropped to the person - rooms and furniture in the reference
   leak into the render as content.
3. Replace is already ON: two 5-second windows, SAM3 auto-masks, render = `anchor`,
   audio policy = `source`, lead 12, grow 1, feather 1.
4. Use `Test mask` on a window and PICK the subject with click points. Points are far
   more reliable than text - the `the woman` prompt in `sam_prompts` is only a fallback.
   Copy the points to the other windows, then render.
5. Watch the console: `FELL BACK to plain RV2V` means the mask failed for that window
   and the render will not replace anything.

## Which channel owns the outfit

The RefMod reference carries everything its images show - face, clothing, rooms. If the
outfit should come from the reference, keep `wardrobe:` matching it. If the outfit must
come from the prompt, crop the mod images so they do not show a conflicting outfit.

## Perf section

`verbose_logging` prints the pack's own DEBUG diagnostics for a run (phase timings,
cache decisions, SAM3 attempts, reference counts). `MINIMAX_DIRECTOR_VERBOSE=1/0`
forces it on or off server-wide.

widgets_values_named.text:
# RefMod identity + wardrobe - how to use this workflow

## Quick start

1. `Load H3 RefMods` slot 1 = your character mod. `strength_1` 1.0, `copies_1` 2.
2. Write the outfit in the `wardrobe:` section of every segment prompt, or supply a
   clothing picture and tag it (see Clothing below).
3. Run ONE segment first. Judge the face and the outfit before committing to all three.

## Which source owns which attribute

| Source | Supplies | Never supplies |
| --- | --- | --- |
| H3 RefMod (`elf_girl`) | face, hair, build | clothing |
| `wardrobe:` text | the outfit | identity |
| a `<Picture n>` picture | whatever it shows - strongly | nothing. It is not selective. |

H3 does not bind a reference to a subject. Every reference influences the whole frame,
so each source needs its job stated in the prompt. That statement is what stops an
outfit photo from handing you its model's face.

## Identity

The mod carries identity well and clothing not at all. That split is physical, not a
bug: the saved latent is roughly a 96x54 thumbnail per frame. 96x54 holds face
structure (low frequency). It cannot hold a garment's cut, seams or trim.

What to write - one line in `subject_definitions`, in every segment:

    Identity lock: her face, hair and build are locked to the attached character
    reference and stay identical in every frame and every shot - never a different
    woman.

If the face still drifts, add 2-3 CONCRETE words to that line - hair colour, ear shape,
build. Feature words are what actually fight the model's own default face; a pure
"stay identical" instruction is much weaker.

Knobs that matter, in order of effect:

| Knob | Where | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `strength_1` | Load H3 RefMods | 1.0 = full reference (official behaviour). Below 1.0 the reference is blurred toward a softened copy of itself and identity fades smoothly - a fade dial, not a free win. |
| `copies_1` | Load H3 RefMods | 2-3 is the sweet spot. Each copy costs its full token count in every DiT block. |
| `retention` | Apply H3 RefMod | Master multiplier on top of every `strength_N`. MiniMax levels: 1.0 fully preserved, 0.7 partial, 0.4 attribute transfer (style, not identity), 0.15 weak. |
| `curve_direction` | RefMod Step Curve | Envelope over the DENOISE steps. `concept_at_end` holds the reference at full strength in the late steps, where facial detail is refined. Targeted fix for late drift. |

Do not confuse the two curves. `Apply H3 RefMod`'s `curve_direction` chooses WHICH
REFERENCE FRAMES dominate. `MiniMaxH3RefModStepCurve`'s chooses WHICH DENOISE STEPS get
the reference.

## Clothing

### Text channel - works today, no wiring

Describe the outfit in the `wardrobe:` section of each segment prompt:

    wardrobe:
    Her outfit is set by this description and not by the character reference: a fitted
    dark-teal trail-running tank top, black compression shorts with a thin reflective
    stripe, and a worn olive utility belt.

The mod will not fight you over this, because it is not carrying clothing.

### Image channel - stronger, but it is not selective

A picture reference is full resolution through H3's native reference path, which is
built to copy the subject out of an image. Excellent for a garment, dangerous for
everything else.

Tag numbering is 1-based (`<Picture index + 1>`). Count the reference images in that
segment. Your RefMod does NOT take a tag slot - RefMod blocks are unnamed latents - so a
lone clothing picture is always `<Picture 1>`.

Use it, and name the boundary:

    wardrobe:
    Her clothing comes from <Picture 1>. Reproduce the garment only - the same colour,
    fabric, cut and length. <Picture 1> must not supply a face, hair, body shape, skin
    tone, background or framing, and must not supply any other character visible in that
    image. The character reference supplies her face, hair and build and must not supply
    clothing.

What actually happens in practice: a character sheet is the worst possible input, because
a character sheet IS an identity reference - and one with several characters on it is
worse still. Expect the face, body and pose to be taken from it. Text cannot out-argue a
full-resolution identity reference.

Ranked fixes:

1. Crop the reference to the garment alone. No face in the picture means no face to copy.
   The only option that removes the failure instead of negotiating with it.
2. Deliver the outfit as a second RefMod on loader slot 2 at `strength_2` around 0.4 -
   MiniMax's documented "attribute transfer (keep style/attributes, not identity)" level -
   with identity at `strength_1` 1.0. Both sources are then the same kind of signal and
   each has its own weight. `MiniMaxH3RefModExtract` has a `mask` input, so the head can
   be masked out during extraction instead of cropped by hand.
3. `MiniMaxH3RefModStepCurve` at `concept_at_end` holds identity late. This tips the
   balance toward the mod but does not stop the picture's face being copied.

Do not expect a second RefMod to split attributes by itself. Refs are not bound to
subjects, so an outfit mod bleeds into the face unless its `strength` is low.

## Settings this workflow ships with

| Setting | Value | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `copies_1` | 2 | doubles the reference's attention mass |
| `strength_1` | 1.0 | full reference, official behaviour |
| `retention` | 1.0 | no master attenuation |
| SLA `enabled` | false | SLA drops ~90% of attention blocks after step 1 - the largest fidelity loss in the stack, and a latent-only reference suffers first |
| SLA `reference_protection` | Light | pre-set for if you switch SLA back on |
| `context_length` | 44 | only the first N frames of a segment are pinned to the previous segment's real output; the rest is free generation |
| `wardrobe:` section | all 3 segments | the clothing channel |

`reference_protection = Light` is APPROXIMATED on the `comfy_kitchen` engine (a
query-averaged global ranking). `engine = triton` gives the exact per-query-block version.

## If something is wrong

**Face drifts to a generic woman.** Add concrete identity words to the `Identity lock:`
line first. Then check `copies_1` is 2 and `strength_1` is 1.0. Then add
`MiniMaxH3RefModStepCurve` with `concept_at_end`.

**Clothing is ignored.** Check the tag number matches the picture's position. Then crop
the reference to the garment. Then try the RefMod route at `strength_2` 0.4.

**Clothing image takes over the face.** Expected with a face-bearing reference. Crop it,
or move to the RefMod route.

**Whole render is mush.** Drop `copies_1` back to 1, or re-enable SLA as a sanity check.
`strength` below 1.0 blurs the reference rather than reducing it.

## Bisect - one lever at a time, same seed

1. `copies_1` back to 1
2. SLA `enabled` back to true
3. `context_length` back to 22
4. delete the `Identity lock:` line

Whichever one brings the problem back is the cause.

## Notes

- `MiniMaxH3RefModTextEncode` is the labelled route (`<Picture 1> = elf_girl`), but the
  Director keeps only the raw reference blocks from a connected conditioning and discards
  the rest, so that labelling cannot reach it. Use picture refs when you want tags.
- The Director has no `reference_image_N` inputs. `MiniMaxH3MotionDirectorConditioning`
  does, one per picture, mapping `reference_image_{i}` to `<Picture {i+1}>`.
- Python changes need a ComfyUI restart. JS changes only need a hard refresh.

## For reference: the official HearmemanAI RefMod example

Simpler than this workflow in every way: ONE 5-second shot (124 frames), no chaining, no
attention sparsity, and the clean `minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot` at `simple` /
20 steps. It runs `retention 0.85` x `strength 0.9` = 0.765 - WEAKER than this workflow -
so "the reference is too weak" is not the first thing to suspect. Its prompt gives the
subject a short label and an outfit ("realistic person, natural human appearance, casual
stylish outfit"), and it keeps a disabled character-LoRA slot wired in as a companion to
the mod.

# Diffusion Model Pipeline / LoRA Switch Config

This workflow routes between three model paths (FL2VA T2V/I2V, REF2VA, and H3 Fast Video), each with its own LoRA and sampling settings, feeding into a single **Model Switch** node for selection at runtime.

## Model #1 - FL2VA (T2V/I2V)

- **Base model**: `minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned_int8...`
- **LoRA**: `minimax_h3_fl2v_turbo_4step_v1.0_768p_comfyui_bf...` (strength: 1.00)
- **Sampling shift**: Video 6.00 / Audio 3.00

## Model #2 - REF2VA

- **Base model**: `minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int...`
- **LoRA**: `minimax_h3_ref2v_turbo_4step_v0.1_comfyui_bf16.sa...` (strength: 1.00)
- **Sampling shift**: Video 12.00 / Audio 3.00

## Model #3 - H3 Fast Video

- **Base model**: `minimax_h3_fastvideo_vsa_dat...`
- **LoRA**: bypassed by default (this model is already a speed-optimized diffusion model, so no turbo LoRA is needed)
- **Optional**: users can un-bypass the LoRA node to stack the FL2VA turbo LoRA on top of the fast video model. This may speed things up further but will likely introduce quality deficits.
- **Sampling shift**: Video 12.00 / Audio 3.00

## Model Switch

- **Node**: Impact-Pack Model Switch
- **Inputs**: up to 5 model inputs (input1–input5), only inputs 1–3 populated here
- **select**: 1 (currently routing Model #1)
- **sel_mode**: `select_on_execution`

## Notes

- Each path uses `ModelSamplingMiniMax` to set video/audio shift values before hitting the switch.
- Feeds into KSamplerSelect (sampler: `er_sde`) and BasicScheduler (scheduler: `simple`) downstream.
- ## IMPORTANT: IF you are switching between models using the switch node, make sure you change the MODEL TYPE in the DIRECTOR node configuration.

extra.description: SFW ref2va (Reference to Video) example: one continuous golden-hour forest run, 3 segments x 7s (21s total @24fps). Subject 1 is an athletic elf woman sprinting through dense forest, clearing a creek and a log, vaulting onto a high branch, then stopping at a cliff edge to view the vast forest. Dynamic cinematic camera (orbit / tracking / low-angle pan). No dialogue, no music - only exertion breaths, movement grunts, clothes rustle, footfalls, forest ambience. To use: upload a headshot as Picture 1 and a full-body character sheet as Picture 2 in the Director's common references, then generate (Export all). Requires the H3 REF2VA model selected on the ImpactSwitch (select 2 = MODEL_2 / ref2va path).
